notes: The schematic labels the input as pin 2, but the manual text and the circuit image use pin 4. I used pin 4.
The resistor is 10k ohm, entered as value=10000.

The breadboard image is drawn upside-down relative to the catalogue naming. The half with rows a-e (and the rails beside it) is at the bottom of the image, so I used bank 't' and rails tp/tn for it. Rows f-j are bank 'b'.

The pushbutton straddles the centre gap at columns 6 and 8. I assumed the joined side pairs run along each column. So side 1 is column 6 (1.l at 6b.f, 1.r at 6t.e) and side 2 is column 8 (2.l at 8b.f, 2.r at 8t.e).
Pin 4 and the resistor's top leg share column 6. A wire from 5V in the + rail reaches column 8, so pressing the button joins pin 4 to 5V. The resistor's other end goes to the ground (-) rail.
Exact rail hole numbers (tp.3, tn.2, tp.8, tn.6) are estimated from the image.
